chunks: As for the one who thinks that the situation is confusing to him

he does not know whether Imam Hasan Askari (peace be upon him) did have a son or not, and that he will adhere to the Imamate of Imam Hasan Askari (peace be upon him) until it is proved that he had a son, his assertion is invalid, because we proved the Imamate of Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him) and we proved that the Imams are twelve.

Retaining these proofs in mind, one need not be confused, but rather, it is most convincing that Hasan’s son is the Imam. It is further strengthened by our proofs that no Imam passes away until he sires an heir and sees his legatee.
And it is confirmed by what has been narrated:

key_terms.ابْنِ الْحَسَنِ: Ibn al-Hasan (Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, the 11th Imam)

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars prove the Imamate of Imam Hasan al-Askari's son despite doubts about his birth?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi reinforces the doctrine of *al-Ghaybah al-Kubra* by asserting that the Imamate of Imam Hasan al-Askari’s son is not merely probable but definitive (*qat’i*), countering those who remained in suspense. He grounds this certainty in the principle that an Imam does not pass away without an heir, thereby ensuring the continuity of the twelve Imams and validating the transition to the era of the Hidden Imam.
